steps.name: Teach
steps.text: You're always looking out to sea when you're alone.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: When I was but a wee babe, you'd pick me up, point out into the distance, and tell me that if I kept going that-a-ways, I'd see an ocean bluer than the sky above.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: That was fifty years ago.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: There's things that happened a hundred years ago you still haven't forgotten, señora.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Oh, my little perlita, if you had captained a ship across the churning waves like I once had, seen lightning crash into lightning between the clouds, heard the unending peals of thunder...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: You'd never forget a moment of it your entire life either.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: I'm mighty curious, though, what's this sea the old folks keep going on about really like?

spans.text: I'm mighty curious, though, what's this sea the old folks keep going on about

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: I've lived in this Flat my whole life, so I don't get it at all, no matter how much I rack my brains.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Before my old man died, he'd talk day in day out about going out to sea, about how he followed you and Captain Cruz in filling your holds with treasure—so full your ships would be low in the water.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Your father was the nimblest topman I've ever seen. He'd climb masts like he was going for a stroll in a garden.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Shame there's not many sailors left who've actually seen the sea for themselves.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: And that's my biggest worry, señora. Even with the compass leading the way, we lack seasoned sailors.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: When it comes to the sea, Perlita, we are all reckless, ignorant children.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: *Sigh* ...Nowadays, it's starting to feel like even heading out into the Flat's more trouble than it's worth.

spans.text: *Sigh* ...Nowadays, it's starting to feel like even heading out into the

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: A little fowlbeast told me that a particularly astounding fellow has come to Aarón, and in the process cut off nearly all our trade routes.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Have they finally decided to take us seriously?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: He managed to sniff out all the sites we use to contact the caravans like some kinda beckbeast. Few decades ago, the useless bastards in town couldn't even spot our footprints.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: *Sigh*... Stealing the compass out from under the noses of a massive garrison. To the Inquisition, it might as well have been both humiliation and provocation.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: They'll do whatever they can to find us. It won't be easy.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: We're running out of time, and the boy won't budge... What do we do, señora?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: What if he's telling the truth? That he's not an alchemist?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I am absolutely certain he is one, Perlita.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: The coin on him has the symbols for 'salt' and 'water' on its faces. A set of symbols particular to the school of alchemy. And that particular combination means 'look to the sea for life'.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I am familiar with the coin's former owner, Aulus. He was the most talented of the alchemists.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Moreover, the boy has the same style of swordplay as him. Even their speech has similarities as well.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Even if they knew each other, that doesn't mean he taught him anything. The coin could've been a gift.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: No. If Aulus gave that to someone, it can only mean he had unusually high expectations for him.

spans.text: to someone, it can only mean he had unusually high expectations for him.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: According to their traditions, the coin can only be passed from teacher to student.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: So why won't he admit it, then?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: That puzzles me as well. I've already made it perfectly clear he has nothing to fear if he cooperates...
Young Isidro bites down on the root of his tooth with great force, but he cannot stem the flow of stinging pain bubbling up from his gum.
Before him, a former classmate's corpse lies under the foot of his mentor.
The corpse's long-cold limbs are lined with an azure mucus that makes him retch.
Through the tears in his eyes, a gentle voice like flowing water pierces the depths of his heart.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: Why do you wipe away your tears, Isidro?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You killed him...

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: The sea and the land are as one. To mix them together is nothing more than erasing the barriers between them.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: He decided, of his own free will, to embrace the salt and water flowing within his own body, to share all of his existence with us.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: Be not afraid, be not hateful, derisive, loathing... Shut not the windows, bar not the doors, close not your heart. No longer shall there be polluted blood or shameful pain.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: There will come a day when all will give their all to each other.
Suddenly, the corpse on the floor jerks like a fin out of water, letting out a gurgle of what sounds like grief, before falling flat once more.
Isidro watches the corpse's eyelids slowly lift, revealing the eyes of some unfamiliar creature.
Its lips open wide, and a voice, human yet inhuman, warbles out.
'You are... the same... as me...'

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: No—!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I will never... I will never be like you...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I won't...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mm-ph!

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Flops about)

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Hmm...?

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Claps fins together)

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Nibbles ferociously)

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Ow! What are you doing?!
Nene twists around his leg, trying to use its rotund body to cover his foot.
A variety of sounds leak into the shed from his surroundings. Some weeping, some arguing, but mostly cursing.
Isidro hopes they aren't cursing at him. Wait... He freezes in place as the gears in his subconscious mind begin to turn.
He sticks out his head. No guard outside his door. How unusual.
A line of people walk through the middle of the haven, their heads hung low, their clothes smeared with blood.
Those at the back of the line are dragging planks behind them, with people sporting heinous wounds lying atop them. The wounds are so deep their bones are visible, bandaged only with rags.
Their blood has soaked into the planks, leaving behind long red streaks on the white salt.
Only the occasional gasp stands as proof that they still live.

steps.name: Dismayed Woman
steps.text: Only half of 'em made it back...

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Dismayed Woman
steps.text: What... What happened out there?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: The Inquisition capullos ambushed us at dawn on the only road out. A lot of our mates gave their lives to see us live... Took everything we had to escape.

steps.name: Sad Man
steps.text: The townsfolk don't have salt ships. How'd they get deep enough into the Flat to even find you?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Who knows?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: They're like ghosts, like they don't feel pain. They don't even fall down if you cut them open. They just get right back to attacking you instead.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (Whispers) The clerics in town barely knew the blade from the hilt... How could they pull off something like this?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Oh, there you are, Teach. Where's the rest of your men? Managed to get done what needed doing?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Heavy losses, just like you. There's another crew I haven't heard a peep from either.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...If this goes on, we won't even have enough men to continue salvaging.
Teach is about to say something when she spots Isidro among the crowd.
She walks over, grabs him, and drags him to Rus.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: How'd you get out?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: No guard at the door.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Bring him with you.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Aye.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: I say nay.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I'm saying nay too. This is your problem. I'm not getting involved.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: If you want to eat, you have to work, chaval. If not alchemy, then you'll have to offer something else.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Why not just let me go already?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Don't even think about it. Best prepare yourself to spend the rest of your days here. We're sorely low on manpower.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Stop pulling me.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Morning of the day after tomorrow, Rus, you bring the boy here. I'll go tell the boss.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: What is even going on right now?

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mm-ph!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You want to come along too?

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Nods furiously)

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Gnaws fin indignantly)

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Put the luggage down here, Leaf.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Wait up, Weedy!

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: I don't understand... Why did you bring so much stuff with you?

spans.text: you bring so much stuff with you?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I haven't seen Thorns in a while, right? As his best friend, it's only natural I have a few things to give him.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: You could've let Leaf carry them.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Why bother, when this is barely any—

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Mierda, the box broke open.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: *Sigh* Help tidy this stuff up, Leaf.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: What a big bag... Cleanser, lotion... Oof, that's heavy! Why so many skincare products?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: How else am I supposed to protect myself from this scorching sun? I'm not having a repeat of the tragedy from my last holiday.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Holiday? Aren't we here to find Thorns after he went missing?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Bah, he's a big boy now, he can handle getting a little lost. Let's see, what's in this bag here... Oh right, clothes.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Do you really need an entire suitcase full of outfits for this mission?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: As a representative of Rhodes Island, it's very important that I maintain a certain image.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Wait, so which of these were you giving to Thorns?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That package there, the one you're stepping on!

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Sunscreen... Waterproof, cooling, whitening... Does he really need any of this?

spans.text: Sunscreen... Waterproof, cooling, whitening... Does he

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: What kind of friend would I be if I let him burn to a crisp?

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: ...Well, you know him better, so if you say so.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hey, careful with those, watch what you're throwing!

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Someone's coming. We shouldn't block the street.

steps.name: Pious Townsperson
steps.text: Will you be holding a sermon for us tonight, Señor Alguacil?

steps.name: Pious Townsperson
steps.text: Also, I must thank you! My wife used to sneak into the kitchen every night to eat the grain we had stored away, while keeping to the teachings against gluttony by day.

steps.name: Pious Townsperson
steps.text: But ever since hearing you preach, she hasn't sinned even once! Your teachings have cleansed her soul, and for that, I am grateful beyond words!

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I merely shared with everyone all my worldly possessions...

steps.name: Pious Townsperson
steps.text: You... You are far too humble, señor.

steps.name: Grateful Townsperson
steps.text: Señor Alguacil, please, allow me to hold your hand. Such frightful events have happened in Aarón lately, and I'm terribly afraid...

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: You may, if it might bring you comfort.

steps.name: Sincere Townsperson
steps.text: Wh—While I have never sinned, I was wondering if you could...

steps.name: Sincere Townsperson
steps.text: If you could lay your hand atop my head...

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Alright, no crowding, one at a time!

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Control yourselves! Think about your request before your turn comes! Do not take up too much of the Alguacil's time!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: (Whispers) The locals here seem a little... odd...

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: (Whispers) Probably because they trust in the Inquisition.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: (Whispers) Maybe...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I wonder who's in charge here.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: May I help the two of you?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Ah, that would be amazing! What should I call you, amigo?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Anastasio is my name.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: (Whispers) This dude's really popular...

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: (Whispers) That's for sure. Everyone who sees him stops to greet him.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Calificador Silver is waiting inside. Pray, enter.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Ah, the burden of those cursed with charm. I know it all too well, amigo.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: ...Pardon?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Is this man your...?

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Oh, we're just colleagues. Honestly, I barely know him.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: *Ahem* I am afraid we do not have what we need to hold a proper reception for you, my guests.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: The town granary was recently burnt down by bandits, so I'm afraid we're all going a bit hungry before the next caravan arrives.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Don't worry about it, we brought our own food.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I am truly sorry for this.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: I believe we have yet to formally introduce ourselves?

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: This is Field Operator Elysium, and I'm Engineering Operator Weedy, both from Rhodes Island Pharmaceuticals.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: You're an engineer, then?

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Yes, I am.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Are you familiar with the mechanics behind wind-powered light landships?

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Well, my specialty is bioengineering, so I can't say I'm too familiar with mechanical engineering. However, based on my limited knowledge, I'd say it would be difficult to realize.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: It's different from seaborne ships. If the materials aren't robust enough, the ship will fall apart the moment it tries to move.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: (Impatiently blows at his red streak of hair)

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: What if we used steel for the keel?

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: I'm afraid that would make them too heavy. That's precisely why it's difficult to make wind-powered ones.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Then would you say making such a landship is near impossible?

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: No, I'm sure someone could come up with a design. Once you manage to work out the kinks, the actual construction shouldn't be too difficult.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Well, if we're talking about today's Iberia trapped in its own web... It wouldn't be much more difficult than making a traditional landship.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: (Impatiently waves his hands)

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Look, I'm terribly sorry, but shouldn't we, uh, talk business first?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: For example, the whereabouts of my friend...

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Dios mio, forgive me! I got carried away. Could you describe him for me?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That's crazy, there's no way!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: There's no way he'd do something like that!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Calm down, Señor Elysium. I am simply stating the facts.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: What you're saying is that a Rhodes Island operator colluded with bandits from the Salt Flat, both in stealing the corpses of the townspeople and arranging a rescue from his execution.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: He never mentioned Rhodes Island during the interrogation... but the crimes are real.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Ahem. There must be some sort of misunderstanding here.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I regret to inform you that all the information we have points towards him being this criminal.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mm-ph!

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Wriggles about)

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I said, stop following me already.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Show Nene a little more respect, chaval.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I'm treating it the way I would treat any of you.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Which clearly isn't respectful enough. Nene's far more useful than you are.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I thought it was your emergency rations.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: It's practically the boss's heart and soul! Who'd dare harm a scale on its head?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Besides, it's got far sharper senses than us out in the Flat. How else are we supposed to find anything under all that salt?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What are you looking for?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Hah, what else? Relics of the Golden Age. Sometimes high-tech curios, sometimes luxury items or whatever else. Good money either way.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: But doesn't the Inquisition crack down on these sorts of excavations for Golden Age antiques?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: They may not like it, but the caravans sneaking into Iberia sure do. We trade these trinkets for water and supplies. It beats begging, that's for sure.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: So it's smuggling...

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Don't give me that look. You think it's easy, living out here?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: But you, chaval...

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Every last one of the materials we got you for your alchemy, down to the smallest finbone, was bought by the blood, sweat, and tears of our crew.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...So think it over. If you know you can't do it, then don't waste our booty.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What are you suggesting?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Do a little hoo-hah during your alchemy, show the boss you failed, and give her a reason to back down from this madness.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (Whispers) Can't you just, I don't know, let me go?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Also, why not tell her that yourself?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Don't want her to think we're against the plan. We respect her... fear her.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Fear? Well, I suppose she is an amazing fighter.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: There're better reasons to be afraid of her.
Juana stops in her tracks, as though she sensed something in the wind.
She looks behind her. She sees no trace of any living creature, besides her own footprints left on the desolate Salt Flat.
She breathes a sigh of relief and continues onwards. There is a giant skeleton in front of her, and below it, a dark shadow.
She steps into the shadow, and disappears.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: There was a mutiny, back in the day, but only a few old bastards still remember it.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Someone said—in front of everyone—that she'd been working with the sea monsters, that she offered her entire crew up for freakish strength and longevity.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You mean the Seaborn?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Whatever they're called. At the time, the sea had only just retreated, and the monsters were still running wild. It was thanks to Captain Cruz and his crew risking life and limb that most of 'em were cleared out.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: And Captain Cruz... They all died out in the Flat. Well, almost all. Juana was the only one to come back.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: And when she did, she took over the entire fleet. Anyone who didn't wanna follow her ended up dying, one by one. On hunting trips or in Inquisition ambushes.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You said these were just rumors.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...Even Teach was but a lass when this all went down.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: So you think she isn't actually trying to fix the compass to help everyone find a way out?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Mayhaps... Could be part of a much bigger plan. Nobody knows what she really wants.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Are you the only one who suspects her, Señor Rus?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...There's a few of us.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What about Señor Javier?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: No, that boy has never doubted her for a second.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: She's taken care of him so long, he sees her as a mother. She took him under her wing after his mother died.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Those Seaborn in the rumors... Have any of the sailors ever seen one?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Nope... Not a one.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mmp...Mmph!

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: *Glub*—!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What's its problem?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Hah, looks like Nene found something.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Stow the sails, you scallywags! Drop anchor! We're setting down!

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: You heard him! Get digging!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Remember to bring your shovel and your sword, chaval. Don't even think about running. I'll have someone keep an eye on you.
